_comment: Vetted, human-verified exceptions for tools/ci/reconcile-assertion-ledgers.py. Every entry names the evidence a reader can re-check; there is no unexplained entry. Keyed by (ledger file, cited file, cited line) exactly as the ledger's own first table column reads it -- do not add an entry without reading both the ledger's own prose and the source line(s) involved.

equivalences.reason: guard-line-vs-assert-line citation convention (§1b): the ledger's first column cites the shared aabb_intersection guard's own production line (tools.rs:68, `if min[0] >= max[0] || min[1] >= max[1] || min[2] >= max[2]`) once per axis-isolating test (rows suffixed (x)/(y)/(z)), rather than each test's own assert!(...).is_empty()) line. The three real scanner sites those tests exercise are tools.rs:259 (boxes_that_only_touch_do_not_intersect), tools.rs:271 (boxes_that_only_touch_on_y_do_not_intersect), tools.rs:283 (boxes_that_only_touch_on_z_do_not_intersect) -- confirmed by reading the ledger's own §1b prose (which states this explicitly: 'tools.rs:259,271,283 are the same physical lines as existing rows tools.rs:68 (x)/(y)/(z), not new sites') and by reading tools.rs itself to verify each test's body and its one assert! line. Naive file:line matching manufactures three false orphans here; this is the one instance of the guard-line-citation trap this instrument was asked to encode.

guard-line-vs-assert-line citation convention, same shape as tools.rs:68 above: the ledger's row cites PositionConstraint::new's `model.link_model(link_name)?` guard (position.rs:165) directly, since that is what this round's isolating mutation actually neutralized, rather than the two decide.rs tests that exercise it. Those two tests are new_rejects_unknown_link (decide.rs:530, assert_err_mentions call at decide.rs:534) and new_rejects_unresolvable_mobile_frame (decide.rs:549, assert_err_mentions call at decide.rs:553) -- confirmed by reading both test bodies and the ledger's own prose at doc/assertion-discrimination-ledger-p1-robotmodel.md:262, which names both test functions and the mutation run against each. Both decide.rs:534 and :553 are already independently matched via this same ledger's Round 13 via:assert_err_mentions row; this entry only resolves the separate guard-line citation, it does not double-count the sites.

Historical row recording a scanner false positive that has since been fixed at source, so the site it names no longer exists to be matched. The line was `assert!(tree.insert_ray(origin, end, None, false))`, which the old eq_none grammar scored as an Option-absence comparison although the `None` is insert_ray's `max_range: Option<f64>` argument. `6792ef1` (tools(ci): score None/Err only as an operand of an equality macro) narrowed the grammar, so the scanner emits nothing there now -- verified by `count-coarse-assertions.py | rg 'tree.rs:18(0[0-9]|1[0-9])'` returning no rows, the line itself having drifted to tree.rs:1809. The citation stays because it is the evidence for the ledger's 72 -> 71 correction; it is not a coverage gap.

The scanner does emit this site, but tagged `helper_body` (`crates/moveit-distance-field/tests/oracle_parity.rs:264:is_none:helper_body:assert!(actual.voxel.is_none(), ...)`), and this sweep's corpus is the scanner's output *excluding* helper_body -- so it is outside the population by definition, not missing from it. Its two call sites (oracle_parity.rs:296,304) are separately accounted by the same ledger's `via:check_scenario` row, and the helper body carries its own round-2 bite-check comment covering nearest_cell's five `voxel: None` return sites.
